name: time
description: Module 23: time — the NTP offset and delay arithmetic, a server that is 5 minutes wrong, what asymmetric delay does to the estimate, how chrony out-votes a falseticker, and TLS certificate checks with a skewed clock

checks.name: the four timestamps: t1 client send, t2 server receive, t3 server send, t4 client receive; offset = ((t2−t1)+(t3−t4))/2 and delay = (t4−t1)−(t3−t2). With 10 ms each way and the same clock: offset ≈ 0, delay ≈ 20 ms
expect_contains: median of 5: offset +0.0 ms (+0.00 s), delay 2

checks.name: a server whose clock is 5 minutes ahead: the offset says so (+300 000 ms) and the delay is unaffected

asymmetric path, same clocks: 10 ms in, 50 ms out — the formula assumes both halves are equal, so it reports a −20 ms offset that is not there; the error is half the asymmetry and can never exceed delay/2 (≈ 30 ms)

chronyd -Q measures without touching the clock (here every namespace shares one kernel clock, so nothing may set it): one good server, then the 5-minutes-ahead server alone — a single source is believed whatever it says
run: chronyd -Q -u root -f /dev/null 'server 198.18.234.11 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0' 2>&1 | grep -o 'System clock wrong.*'; chronyd -Q -u root -f /dev/null 'server 198.18.234.66 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0' 2>&1 | grep -o 'System clock wrong.*'

checks.name: three sources, one 5 minutes off: chrony's selection finds the two that agree, marks the odd one a falseticker (x) and synchronises to a good one (*); note chronyc's sign: −300 s means the source is ahead
run:
mkdir -m 700 -p ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three; printf 'server 198.18.234.11 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0
server 198.18.234.12 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0
server 198.18.234.66 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0
bindcmdaddress ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.sock
pidfile ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.pid
' > ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chrony.conf; chronyd -x -u root -f ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chrony.conf -l ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.log; sleep 8; chronyc -h ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.sock -n sources | tail -n +2; chronyc -h ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.sock -n tracking | sed -n '1,2p'; kill $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.pid); sleep 0.3; echo '--- chronyd log:'; grep -E 'falseticker|Selected source|majority' ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-three/chronyd.log | cut -d' ' -f2- | sort | uniq -c

checks.name: two sources that disagree: neither has a majority, both are marked x and chrony does not synchronise at all ('no majority') — use at least three, preferably four, independent sources; the asymmetric server is shown alongside (noselect): +20 ms, but inside its ±error bound
run:
mkdir -m 700 -p ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two; printf 'server 198.18.234.11 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0
server 198.18.234.66 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0
server 198.18.234.40 iburst minpoll 0 maxpoll 0 noselect
bindcmdaddress ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.sock
pidfile ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.pid
' > ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chrony.conf; chronyd -x -u root -f ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chrony.conf -l ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.log; sleep 8; chronyc -h ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.sock -n sources | tail -n +2; chronyc -h ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.sock -n tracking | sed -n '1,2p'; kill $(cat ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.pid); sleep 0.3; echo '--- chronyd log:'; grep -E 'falseticker|Selected source|majority' ${EVIDENCE}/chrony-two/chronyd.log | cut -d' ' -f2- | sort | uniq -c

checks.name: TLS with a wrong clock: the certificate is valid from 1 h ago for 30 days; a client clock 2 h behind or 31 days ahead rejects it with the error users report as 'your connection is not private'
run: for o in 0s -30m -2h 696h 744h; do ${BIN}/edgelab tlsclock -connect 198.18.234.80:443 -servername web.time.test -cafile ${EVIDENCE}/webpki/ca.pem -offset $o; done
expect_contains: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time
